title: US concerns hold up AI chip deliveries to Gulf
key_facts: US advanced AI-chip exports to Gulf companies are delayed by investment negotiations, regulatory hurdles, infrastructure limits and US concern about leakage to China, according to analysts.
Commerce authorised 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips a year ago for G42 (UAE) and Humain (Saudi Arabia); both have received some but not all.
In July the Bureau of Industry and Security eased restrictions on chip sales to the UAE, moving it to the A:5 group of allies and partners.
Nazak Nikakhtar of law firm Wiley Rein said she thinks Commerce is still waiting, pointing to UAE and Saudi pledges to invest in the US that have only partly materialised.
Humain received its first shipment at the end of December last year (CEO Tareq Amin on LinkedIn); the UAE saw its first batch in May (ambassador Yousef Al Otaiba).
BIS only facilitated direct purchases by G42 and Core42 until 6 April 2027, pending an extension or a move of their headquarters to the US.
Ruth Berry, who leads Nvidia's global policy, said delays may inadvertently boost the appeal of Chinese offerings.
The US departments and Gulf governments contacted for comment; no response is reported.
quote_evidence: US advanced AI-chip exports to Gulf companies are being delayed by investment negotiations, regulatory hurdles, infrastructure constraints and Washington’s concerns over technology leaking to China, analysts have said.
The Commerce department authorised the shipping of 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips to artificial intelligence developers G42 in the UAE and Humain in Saudi Arabia a year ago.

Washington dragging out chips deliveries may inadvertently boost the appeal of competing Chinese offerings, said Ruth Berry, who leads Nvidia’s global policy and is a former State department official.
why_it_matters_hint: Delays in Gulf deliveries show how security conditions and investment pledges shape where US AI chips go.
notes: Analysis piece; reasons come from analysts, officials did not comment.
